abstract: Wheat rust diseases threaten global wheat production, highlighting the need for durable sources of resistance. The Lr67-associated G144R substitution in the sugar transport protein gene TaSTP13-D1 confers broad-spectrum resistance to multiple fungal pathogens. Here, we used an enhanced prime-editing system (ePPEplus) to introduce this resistance-associated substitution into the three TaSTP13 homoeologs in hexaploid wheat. Using the wheat-compatible JWPE1 vector, we achieved editing frequencies of 84 to 92% across the A, B, and D genomes in regenerated T0 plants. Homozygous edits were recovered in all three homoeologs, including one line carrying homozygous edits across all three genomes. Disease assays showed that edited lines had reduced leaf rust severity and fungal biomass compared with susceptible controls. Notably, the line carrying edits in all three homoeologs exhibited the greatest reduction in fungal biomass. These results demonstrate the potential of prime editing to directly introduce resistance-associated alleles into wheat and provide a strategy for accelerating the development of rust-resistant cultivars.

metadata.title: Engineering the Lr67-associated G144R substitution by prime editing enhances leaf rust resistance in wheat

summary: Prime editing introduced the Lr67-associated G144R substitution into all three TaSTP13 homoeologs of wheat, reducing leaf rust severity and fungal biomass.
title: Engineering the Lr67-associated G144R substitution by prime editing enhances leaf rust resistance in wheat
